seoTitle: How to Reconcile a Credit Card in QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Learn how to reconcile a credit card account in QuickBooks Online, including where Intuit moved the Reconcile tool and how to enter your statement correctly.
intro: Credit card reconciliation is what keeps your books aligned with your statement, and QuickBooks Online handles it through one Reconcile screen shared by every account type: bank, credit card, or otherwise. This guide covers opening that screen (Intuit has since moved its main entry point), entering the statement's balances correctly, and adding a finance charge before matching transactions. It's for small business owners and accountants who want a clean monthly close without second-guessing which numbers go where.
prerequisites: The credit card statement, with its ending balance, ending date, and any finance charges
Every transaction from the statement period already entered and categorized in QuickBooks

steps.heading: Open the Reconcile tool
steps.body: Intuit's current help documentation leads with All apps, then Accounting, then Reconcile. Older paths, including the gear icon's Tools column shown here, may still work depending on the account's navigation, but if Reconcile isn't listed under the gear icon anymore, this is why: All apps > Accounting > Reconcile is the route Intuit now documents. Either way, make sure every transaction from the statement period is already entered and categorized before starting.

image.caption: The gear-icon settings menu with Reconcile listed under Tools — Intuit's current help docs instead lead with All apps > Accounting > Reconcile.

steps.heading: Select the credit card account
steps.body: On the Reconcile screen, the first field asks which account to reconcile. Click the Account dropdown and choose the credit card account, not a bank or expense account. The screen is generic across account types, so double-check the selection before entering numbers, especially with a chart of accounts that has several similarly named entries.

image.caption: The Reconcile screen's account selector and statement details section, with a date picker open on the finance charge date field.

steps.heading: Enter the statement details
steps.body:
QuickBooks fills in the Beginning balance automatically from the last reconciliation; leave it unless there's a specific reason to think it's wrong. Type the Statement ending balance exactly as it appears on the statement, along with the Statement ending date. This pair of numbers matters more than anything else on the screen, since every transaction checked off afterward is measured against it.

If the statement includes interest or a finance charge, enter its date and amount in the finance charge section, then pick the right expense account from the dropdown. QuickBooks defaults to whichever account was last used here, so confirm it's the interest expense account, not something unrelated like Depreciation Expense, before moving on. Skipping a finance charge that's on the statement is one of the most common reasons a reconciliation won't balance.

image.caption: The statement details section, with the finance charge fields filled in and an expense account selected.

steps.heading: Start reconciling and match each transaction
steps.body: Click Start reconciling and QuickBooks lists every transaction posted to the account since the last reconciliation. On some plans, the statement file itself can be uploaded for AI-powered matching instead of checking things off by hand; Intuit notes that verifying an uploaded statement can take up to an hour. Otherwise, work down the list checking off each transaction that appears on the statement. QuickBooks tallies a running difference at the bottom, which should reach $0.00 once every real transaction is checked. Many entries already show a suggested match when the card is connected for bank feeds, which speeds this up considerably.

steps.heading: Track down any discrepancy, then finish
steps.body:
If the difference isn't zero once everything matching is checked off, don't force it closed; that buries the error instead of fixing it. Common causes are a transaction entered twice, one missing entirely, or a wrong amount typed in by hand. Sort the transaction list by amount or date to spot duplicates faster, or select Edit info to correct a mistyped ending balance or date without starting over.

Once the difference reads zero, select Finish now, then Done. QuickBooks saves a reconciliation report that can be found later under History by account. Treat that closing balance as locked: editing a reconciled transaction afterward throws off every reconciliation that came after it.

troubleshooting.problem: Reconcile isn't listed under the gear icon anymore
troubleshooting.cause: Intuit's current help documentation routes through All apps > Accounting > Reconcile instead of the gear icon's Tools column that older guides and screenshots show.
troubleshooting.fix: Use All apps > Accounting > Reconcile. If an account still shows Reconcile under the gear icon, that shortcut works too.

troubleshooting.problem: The difference isn't zero after checking off everything that matches
troubleshooting.cause: A transaction was entered twice, one is missing, or an amount was mistyped.
troubleshooting.fix: Sort the list by amount or date to spot the duplicate or gap, or select Edit info to correct the statement's ending balance or date if that's what's wrong.

troubleshooting.problem: A finance charge posts to the wrong expense account
troubleshooting.cause: The expense account dropdown defaults to whichever account was last used in that field, which may not be the interest expense account.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the dropdown before finishing the reconciliation, not after.

faq.question: Why is credit card reconciliation important in QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: Reconciling confirms the records match the actual credit card statement, catching duplicate or missing transactions before they distort expense reporting or taxes.

faq.question: What should I do if a transaction doesn't match my statement?
faq.answer: Leave the reconciliation open and investigate instead of forcing it to balance; sort the transaction list by amount or date to spot a duplicate, a missing entry, or a mistyped figure.

faq.question: Where is the Reconcile tool in QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: Go to All apps, then Accounting, then Reconcile. Some accounts still show a Reconcile shortcut under the gear icon's Tools column, but Intuit's current documentation leads with All apps.

faq.question: Can I edit a transaction after it's been reconciled?
faq.answer: It's possible, but it changes the balance in every reconciliation done after it, so it's best avoided unless redoing subsequent reconciliations is part of the plan.

faq.question: Is this process beginner-friendly for new QuickBooks users?
faq.answer: Yes. The Reconcile screen walks through the same beginning balance, statement ending balance, and finance charge fields regardless of account type, so these steps apply the first time and every time after.
